message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.68,"fairness_assessment":"A structured vote using transparent criteria would treat visibility, long-term club development, and member benefit fairly; no option is clearly dominant, so equal stakeholder input is appropriate.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Supports option A: spend the full budget on an inter-city tournament, buffet, and prizes to increase the club’s visibility.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Supports option B: invest the full budget in educational materials and new chessboards to strengthen training conditions.","influence":0.34},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Supports option C: split the budget between a smaller tournament and equipment purchases as a balanced compromise.","influence":0.33}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"The three options represent legitimate but competing goals: external visibility, internal development, and balance. A social-choice process should rank the options against agreed criteria and allow a compromise outcome, most plausibly option C or a modified hybrid, while preserving the possibility of reviewing results after one budget cycle."}
